history.summary: Historic temple inside Nurpur Fort, Nurpur — one of the few temples in India where Krishna and Meera Bai are worshipped together. Local tradition says the black-marble Krishna idol (worshipped by Meera Bai) and an ashtadhatu Meera idol were brought from Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, as a gift from the Rana of Mewar. FOUNDER CONFLICT: one account credits Raja Jagat Singh of Nurpur (built 1619-1625); another credits Raja Basu (r. 1580-1613) and dates the siege-capture of the idols to 1613. The temple court was decorated with pahari paintings of Krishna leelas (some whitewashed). The fort and temple were damaged by the 1905 Kangra earthquake; the site is ASI-protected. CSV CORRECTIONS: CSV town 'Pathankot' and CSV 'state' 'Pathankot' are both wrong — the temple is in Nurpur, Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh (address: inside Nurpur Fort, Monument Road, Nurpur 176202). State flag: Himachal Pradesh, not Punjab.

name: Nurpur Brij Raj Swami Temple
town_description: Nurpur is a historic town in Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh, about 25 km from Pathankot, named for Mughal queen Nur Jahan who visited in 1622. It is dominated by the ruined Nurpur Fort (built by the Pathania kings of the Dhameri/Nurpur state), and serves as the gateway to the Kangra valley.

travel.road: Inside Nurpur Fort on Monument Road, Nurpur town; reachable by road from Pathankot

visitor_information.best_time: October to June; Janmashtami is the main festival. Avoid heavy monsoon days
